comments.title: Ground-to-Sky Clearance Violations and Structural Encroachments in Electric Easements
comments.comment: Permanent structures, hardscape, and vegetation encroach into electric easements from ground to sky, and no clearance dimensions are shown on the plans to demonstrate compliance.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.10.3 requires 15-foot minimum lateral clearance from overhead distribution conductors, and UCM § 1.10.10.2 prohibits permanent structures, buildings, utilities, landscaping, and other improvements from encroaching ground-to-sky within electric easements. The following violations are present:
• Existing trees overlap electric easement boundaries and overhead electric (OHE) lines along the southern boundary (Sheets 9, 21) with no tree removal or pruning plan demonstrating 15-foot minimum lateral clearance from overhead conductors
• Type III driveway and 6-foot concrete sidewalk cross through the southern 5' Electric Easement (Sheet 9)
• Concrete retaining wall lines encroach into or run parallel within the southern and eastern 5' electric easement boundaries (Sheets 2, 9)
• Concrete retaining wall enclosing the biofiltration/detention pond is drawn entirely within the eastern 5' Electric Easement in the NE corner (Sheets 9, 16)
• Pond perimeter fencing occupies the NE corner easement area alongside the retaining wall (Sheet 9)
• No ground-to-sky clearance dimensions, setback callouts, or compliance notes appear on the site plan or grading plan confirming structures, overhangs, and improvements do not extend into easement areas
comments.sheets: Site Plan (Sheet 9); Plat (Sheet 2); Grading Plan (Sheet 11); Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Sheet 16
comments.applicableArea: 5' Electric Easements along southern and eastern property boundaries; 5' Elec. & Tele. Easement (Vol. 5468, Pg. 883 D.R.T.C.Tx.) on south; 5' Electric Easement (Vol. 69, Pg. 14; Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.Tx.) on east; NE corner detention pond and retaining wall area; southern property boundary overhead electric line corridor; easement areas on east, south, and northeast portions of property
comments.resolution:
• Submit a tree preservation and removal plan demonstrating 15-foot minimum lateral clearance from all overhead conductors along the southern boundary, or identifying specific trees for removal or pruning to achieve compliance with UCM § 1.10.3
• Relocate the Type III driveway, 6-foot concrete sidewalk, concrete retaining walls, and pond perimeter fencing outside all electric easement boundaries, or provide documented evidence (e.g., recorded vacation or modification instrument) that the affected easements have been abandoned or modified
• Add dimension callouts or a compliance note to the site plan (Sheet 9) and grading plan (Sheet 11) confirming ground-to-sky clearance is maintained between all proposed structures, improvements, overhangs, and the boundaries of every electric easement on the property

perRunFindings.comment: Ground-to-sky clearances within electric easements are not maintained or shown. The site plan and grading plan show buildings and site improvements near easement boundaries, but do not dimension vertical clearances or confirm that structures do not encroach from ground to sky within the easement area. Please show (via dimension line or note) that all buildings, structures, utilities, and permanent site improvements maintain ground-to-sky clearance (no vertical encroachment) from easement boundaries, or clarify exactly how close structures approach the easement in both horizontal and vertical directions.
applicableAreas: Electric easement areas and all structures within 15 feet of easement boundaries
perRunFindings.observation: Examined the site plan (Sheet 9) and grading plan (Sheet 11) for any ground-to-sky clearance dimensions or notes. Vision analysis of Sheet 11 confirmed: 'There are no ground-to-sky clearances, structural setback dimensions from buildings to easements, or related clearance notes visible on this sheet.' The site plan shows buildings and site improvements near easement boundaries, but provides NO clearance dimensions from building edges, roof lines, canopies, awnings, structures, or landscaping to the easement boundaries. The grading plan similarly shows no special treatment or clearance zones within easement areas. While the electrical design plan notes that all electric infrastructure is underground (which eliminates the 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance requirement for overhead conductors), UCM § 1.10.10.2 prohibits ground-to-sky encroachment within electric and telecommunications easements for ANY type of structure, site amenity, or permanent improvement.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Although all electric facilities shown on this project are underground distribution, UCM § 1.10.10.2 still prohibits permanent structures, buildings, utilities, site amenities, landscaping, and other improvements from encroaching from ground to sky within electric easements. The requirement protects Austin Energy's right to access, maintain, and potentially upgrade easement areas. The site plan must explicitly show or dimension how much clearance (if any) exists between building footprints, hardscape, and other improvements and the recorded easement boundaries.

perRunFindings.comment: Ground-to-sky clearances within electric easements are not maintained; existing trees, retaining walls, fencing, and other permanent site improvements are shown directly overlapping easement boundaries. Remove all trees within electric easement boundaries or shown within 15 feet of overhead conductors. Relocate concrete retaining walls and pond perimeter fencing outside easement boundaries or provide written approval from Austin Energy for placement within easements. Provide tree removal and landscape modification details demonstrating 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radius clearance from overhead conductors per UCM § 1.10.3.
applicableAreas: Electric easement areas on east, south, and northeast portions of property; areas with overhead electric facilities
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts numerous existing trees (shown as scalloped and dashed circles) overlapping electric easement boundaries. Vision analysis confirms: 'Numerous existing tree symbols (scalloped and dashed circles) are mapped directly overlapping the eastern Greenbelt Access & Use Easement, 15' Easement, and 5' Electric Easement...Tree symbols also heavily overlap the 25' Drainage Easement in the NE corner and the 5' Elec. Easement on the south perimeter.' Additionally, the vision analysis identifies: 'A heavy Concrete Retaining Wall runs continuously inside the North, East, and South perimeters, acting as a physical barrier... A Wood Fence is labeled running along the far East property line...A Pond Perimeter Fence circles the NE corner pond.' Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) notes transformer pads are located in spaces suggesting these facilities sit in unpaved, landscaped, or natural surface areas.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires 7.5 feet minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead conductors within electric easements, and a 15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. Trees within electric easements create permanent obstructions that violate these clearances and restrict Austin Energy's ability to access and maintain overhead and underground facilities. The presence of trees shown directly overlapping easements, combined with the absence of any tree removal or clearing callouts, demonstrates non-compliance.

perRunFindings.comment: Ground-to-sky clearances within electric easements and electric and telecommunications easements (ETE) not maintained; buildings, structures, utilities, site amenities, landscaping, trees, overhead features, or other improvements encroach from ground to sky. Existing trees overlap or are immediately adjacent to overhead electric lines along the southern property boundary, violating the minimum 15-foot lateral clearance required from overhead conductors. Provide a tree preservation and removal plan that either demonstrates 15-foot minimum clearance from overhead conductors will be maintained or identifies trees for removal/pruning to comply with clearance requirements.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary where overhead electric (OHE) lines and existing trees are located
perRunFindings.observation: Vision analysis of Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) explicitly states: 'Existing tree symbols (large circles) do overlap the existing OHE (overhead electric) lines running along the southern boundary.' Vision analysis of Site Plan (Sheet 9) confirms existing trees are shown adjacent to the OHE lines along the southern property line. The Grading Plan (Sheet 11) shows contour lines and existing tree symbols in the area of the OHE lines. The General Notes (Sheet 3) require that 'Austin Energy has the right to prune and/or remove trees...to keep the easements clear' and state that 'Trees: Minimum 15 lateral feet from overhead conductors or equipment.'
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 specifies 'Permanent Clearances From AE Overhead Distribution Lines and Facilities: 7.5 feet minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead conductors' and '15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors.' UCM § 1.10.10.2 addresses ground-to-sky clearances and customer activities in easements. The regulatory overview explicitly requires 'Trees: Minimum 15 lateral feet from overhead conductors or equipment.'

perRunFindings.comment: Concrete retaining walls, Type III driveway, and concrete sidewalk are shown encroaching into the southern and eastern 5' electric easement areas. Relocate all structures and permanent improvements outside the electric easement boundaries, or provide evidence that these easements have been abandoned or modified. Coordinate with Austin Energy to verify easement status.
applicableAreas: southern 5' electric easement boundary
eastern 5' electric easement boundary
southern and eastern property boundaries
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 2 (Plat) and Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depict 5' electric easements along the southern boundary ('5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 883 D.R.T.C.Tx.') and eastern boundary ('5' Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14; Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.Tx.'). On Sheet 9, multiple improvements are drawn directly overlapping or encroaching into these easement boundaries: (1) A Type III Driveway with notation 'Construct Type III Driveway See Detail 1/335-2' crosses completely through the southern 5' electric easement; (2) A 6' Concrete Sidewalk labeled 'Construct 6' Concrete Sidewalk See Dtl 4/335-1' crosses through the southern 5' easement; (3) Concrete Retaining Wall lines overlap and encroach into both the southern and eastern 5' easement areas, running parallel to the easement boundaries.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 explicitly prohibits permanent structures, buildings, overhangs, balconies, canopies, stairways, eaves, awnings, patios, roofed structures, and permanent improvements (including below-grade footings) within electric easements. Driveways, sidewalks, and retaining walls are permanent improvements.

perRunFindings.comment: Concrete retaining wall enclosing the detention pond is located within the 5' Electric Easement and must be removed or relocated outside the easement. No permanent structures are permitted within electric easements where Austin Energy must maintain 24-hour access to facilities.
applicableAreas: 5' Electric Easement along eastern and southern property boundaries
perRunFindings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 9 (Site Plan) identified the concrete retaining wall enclosing the biofiltration/detention pond located in the northeastern corner. The vision tool analysis explicitly states: 'Yes, the Biofiltration/Detention Pond overlaps. The eastern edge of the "Concrete Retaining Wall" enclosing the pond is drawn completely within the 5-foot space between the dashed easement line and the eastern property line.' This retaining wall is a permanent improvement structure (not an electric facility) within the 5' electric easement boundary.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 states: 'No permanent structures, buildings, swimming pools, or improvements (including below-grade footings) are allowed within electric easements.' A concrete retaining wall is explicitly a permanent improvement. The vision analysis confirmed it is within the 5' electric easement.

comments.title: Recorded Easements Not Depicted; Improvements in PUEs Without Approval
comments.comment: Two recorded easements encumbering approximately 0.44 acres are absent from the submitted site plan, and permanent improvements including a detention pond, retaining walls, and fencing are placed within Public Utility Easement boundaries without documented written Austin Energy approval.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.10.10.2 and § 1.5.2.1.L require that Public Utility Easements be kept clear of buildings, structures, utilities, site amenities, landscaping, and other permanent improvements unless written Austin Energy approval has been obtained. Multiple deficiencies are present:
• The Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (0.31 ac, NE interior, Instrument 2010070731) is not depicted on the submitted site plan despite being a perpetual no-build encumbrance; Building 4 is positioned immediately adjacent to this area
• The City of Austin Drainage Easement (0.130 ac, NE corner, Instrument 2011021137) is also absent from the site plan; the detention pond, retaining walls, and pond perimeter fence are placed directly within the 25' Drainage Easement area in the NE corner
• The site plan shows driveways, parking, and other improvements near PUE boundaries with no notation confirming written Austin Energy approval for any improvements within PUEs per UCM § 1.5.2.1.L
• The Landscape Plan does not specify which trees and site amenities will be placed within PUE boundaries, creating unresolvable ambiguity about PUE compliance
comments.sheets: Site Plan (Sheet 9); Grading Plan (Sheet 11); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: All Public Utility Easements on site; 25' Drainage Easement NE corner; Greenbelt Access & Use Easement NE interior; 5' P.U.E. and 7.5' P.U.E. boundaries along north, east, and southeast property boundaries
comments.resolution:
• Add the Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (Instrument 2010070731, 0.31 ac, NE interior) and the City of Austin Drainage Easement (Instrument 2011021137, 0.130 ac, NE corner) to all applicable plan sheets, then re-evaluate proposed building placement (including Building 4) and the detention pond layout against both easement footprints
• Relocate the infiltration/detention pond, concrete retaining walls, and pond perimeter fencing outside all easement boundaries, or provide written approval from Austin Energy and coordination with the City of Austin Watershed Protection Department for any structures remaining within drainage and utility easements
• Add a note on the site plan and landscape plan confirming that written Austin Energy approval has been obtained (per UCM § 1.5.2.1.L) for any improvements, trees, or landscaping proposed within PUE boundaries, and identify the specific improvements covered by that approval
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Resolution of improvements within the City of Austin Drainage Easement (Instrument 2011021137) may involve coordination with the City of Austin Watershed Protection Department in addition to Austin Energy.

perRunFindings.comment: Public Utility Easements are not clearly kept free of buildings, structures, and other improvements. The site plan shows site improvements near PUE boundaries, but provides no notation confirming that any improvements within or adjacent to PUEs have received written approval from Austin Energy per UCM § 1.5.2.1.L. Please either: (1) relocate all improvements outside PUE boundaries, or (2) provide documentation of written Austin Energy approval for any improvements within PUE boundaries and add a note to the site plan confirming this approval.
applicableAreas: All Public Utility Easements on site
perRunFindings.observation: Examined the site plan (Sheet 9) and grading plan (Sheet 11) for improvements within or near Public Utility Easement boundaries. The grading plan (Sheet 11) shows recorded PUE boundaries (e.g., '5' P.U.E.' and '7.5' P.U.E.') depicted as dashed lines. The site plan shows driveways, parking areas, and other site improvements in proximity to PUE boundaries. However, the plans do NOT include any notation indicating that improvements within or adjacent to PUEs have received written approval from Austin Energy per UCM § 1.5.2.1.L.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 and § 1.5.2.1.L establish that customer facilities (buildings, structures, site amenities, utilities, landscaping) shall NOT be installed within PUEs without written approval from Austin Energy. The absence of such notation on the plans means either improvements are being placed in the PUE without approval (a deficiency), or approval exists but was not documented (also a deficiency).

perRunFindings.comment: Public Utility Easements are not kept clear of site improvements; detention pond with retaining walls and fencing are shown directly within the 25' Drainage Easement in the NE corner. Additionally, critical recorded easements (Greenbelt Access & Use Easement and City of Austin Drainage Easement per facts.md) are not depicted on site plan despite being perpetual encumbrances. Revise site plan to: (1) Depict and label all recorded easements including Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (Instrument 2010070731) and City of Austin Drainage Easement (Instrument 2011021137); (2) Remove detention pond, retaining walls, and fencing from within easement boundaries or provide written approval from Austin Energy and City of Austin Watershed Protection; (3) Relocate Building 4 or other structures outside easement buffers; (4) Provide notation on all sheets that improvements have received written AE/City approval if any structures remain within easements.
applicableAreas: Public Utility Easements on north, east, and northeast property; specifically 25' Drainage Easement area and Greenbelt Access & Use Easement
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows Building 4 positioned 27.3' from the east property line, placing it immediately adjacent to the Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (which occupies NE interior per facts.md). Vision analysis confirms: 'An Infiltration/Detention Pond and Concrete Retaining Wall sit directly inside the 25' Drainage Easement in the northeast corner...A Concrete Retaining Wall encircles it and Pond Perimeter Fence.' Facts.md documents that two critical easements are NOT depicted on the submitted site plan: (1) Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (0.31 acres, NE interior—a perpetual no-build zone per recorded Instrument 2010070731); and (2) City of Austin Drainage Easement (0.130 acres, NE corner—per recorded Instrument 2011021137). The combined two easements encumber approximately 0.44 acres (~19% of the 2.16-acre site).
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 and UCM § 1.5.2.1.L require that Public Utility Easements be kept clear of buildings, structures, utilities, site amenities, landscaping, and other permanent improvements without written approval from Austin Energy. The Greenbelt easement is a perpetual no-build zone per the recorded instrument, yet was not depicted on the site plan. Facts.md explicitly states these easements 'must be depicted before approval' and that 'proposed building layout must be evaluated against both easement footprints.'

perRunFindings.comment: Public Utility Easements (PUE) not kept clear of buildings, structures, utilities, site amenities, landscaping, and other improvements. The site plan does not clearly specify which improvements (if any) will be placed within PUE boundaries, nor does it document written Austin Energy approval for any such improvements. Clarify which site amenities, landscaping, and other improvements will be located within PUE boundaries. If any improvements are proposed within PUEs, provide notation on the plans indicating written Austin Energy approval for those specific improvements.
applicableAreas: Public Utility Easements containing or adjacent to electric facilities (north, east, and southeast property boundaries)
perRunFindings.observation: Vision analysis of Site Plan (Sheet 9) shows PUEs along property boundaries and existing trees/landscaping nearby. The Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) shows landscaping features throughout the site. However, the site plan does not provide a detailed specification of which site amenities and landscaping will be placed within PUE boundaries versus outside them. The plans do not include notation of 'written Austin Energy approval' for any improvements within or near PUEs.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.5.2.1.L requires that 'Customer facilities in easements require AE written approval.' UCM § 1.10.10.2 addresses customer activities in utility easements. The site plan must either show that no improvements are planned within PUE boundaries, or provide notation of written AE approval for any landscaping, trees, or other site amenities to be located within PUE areas.

comments.title: Wood Privacy Fence in 5' Electric Easement Requires Removal or License Agreement
comments.comment: A wood privacy fence is shown within the 5' Electric Easements along the eastern and southern property boundaries without documentation that it is removable or that a license agreement from Austin Energy has been obtained.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.10.2 prohibits permanent fencing within electric easements; an exception allows removable wooden fences only under a license agreement if they permit Austin Energy crew and equipment access. The site plan and landscape plan show a wood privacy fence (Keynote H-6) running along the eastern property boundary within the 5' Electric Easement (Vol. 69, Pg. 14; Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.Tx.), and fencing is also shown along the southern 5' Electric Easement (Vol. 5468, Pg. 885). No construction detail designates either fence as removable, and no license agreement from Austin Energy is documented on the plans.
comments.applicableArea: Eastern 5' Electric Easement (Vol. 69, Pg. 14; Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.Tx.) from Building 6 to the eastern property boundary; southern 5' Electric Easement (Vol. 5468, Pg. 885) along the southern property boundary
comments.resolution: Either relocate the wooden privacy fence(s) entirely outside the electric easement boundaries, or: (1) provide construction specifications (detail sheet) confirming the fence is removable and can be readily removed to permit Austin Energy crew and equipment access; and (2) submit an executed license agreement from Austin Energy authorizing placement of the fence within the easement. If the fence remains within the easement under a license, add a plan note on Sheets 9 and 31 referencing the license agreement and confirming removability.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Medium confidence (2/3 runs); reviewer should confirm on Sheet 31 whether Keynote H-6 fence details specify any removable construction or temporary installation provisions.

perRunFindings.comment: A permanent wood privacy fence is shown within the eastern 5' electric easement. Remove the fence from the easement, or if a removable wooden fence is intended, provide documentation of a license agreement from Austin Energy and specifications clearly identifying the fence as removable to permit Austin Energy maintenance access.
applicableAreas: eastern 5' electric easement area near southeast portion of site
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts a line labeled 'Wood Fence' running along the property boundary directly within the eastern 5' Electric Easement area (Vol. 69, Pg. 14; Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.Tx.). The site plan detail references and notes indicate this is a wooden privacy fence as part of the landscaping/site amenity design. A wooden privacy fence is a permanent structure designed to remain in place; it is not removable. The fence is located between Building 6 and the eastern property boundary, directly overlapping the dashed easement line.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 contains an exception: 'Removable wooden fences may be allowed in easements under license agreement if removable to permit Austin Energy crew and equipment access.' However, the prohibition is clear for permanent or masonry fencing. The site plan shows a 'privacy fence,' which by nature and nomenclature is a permanent landscape feature not designed for removal. There is no notation stating the fence is removable or that a license agreement allows its installation.

perRunFindings.comment: If wooden privacy fence is located within the 5' Electric Easement, provide detail sheet specifications confirming it is removable and readily can be removed to permit Austin Energy crew and equipment access. Alternatively, provide executed license agreement from Austin Energy authorizing the fence installation. Permanent fencing is not permitted in electric easements.
applicableAreas: 5' Electric Easement along eastern property boundary
perRunFindings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) identified: 'Wooden Privacy Fence: A line with x marks runs along the eastern boundary, which corresponds to Key Note H-6 (WOODEN PRIVACY FENCE).' The fence is shown running along the eastern property boundary where the 5' Electric Easement is located. The landscape plan does not indicate whether this fence is removable or permanent construction.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 allows: 'Removable wooden fences may be allowed in easements under license agreement if removable to permit Austin Energy crew and equipment access.' However, non-removable or permanent fencing prevents access. The landscape plan shows a wooden privacy fence along the eastern boundary within the electric easement area but provides no specification indicating it is removable or that a license agreement exists.

perRunFindings.comment: Permanent wood fencing is shown within 5-foot electric easements on eastern and southern property boundaries. UCM § 1.10.10.2 permits only removable wooden fences under license agreement. Either: (1) remove fencing from easement boundaries and relocate outside easement areas, (2) replace with removable fence type with notation indicating removable design allowing Austin Energy access, or (3) obtain executed license agreement from Austin Energy permitting the fence type proposed. Provide details showing fence construction and removability certification if fences will remain within easements.
applicableAreas: Wood fencing along eastern and southern property boundaries within 5-foot electric easements
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows fencing lines drawn directly along the eastern and southern property boundaries. These same property boundaries have 5-foot electric easements dedicated to utility use (labeled on Sheet 9 as '5' Electric Easement Vol. 60...' on the east and '5' Elec. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 885...' on the south). The fence lines follow the property boundary, placing them within the 5-foot easement width. Site plan details and notes do not identify these fences as removable, temporary, or specially designed to allow Austin Energy access.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 explicitly allows removable wooden fences within electric easements under a license agreement if they permit Austin Energy crew and equipment access. However, it prohibits permanent or non-removable fencing. The submitted plans do not specify that these fences are removable or designed for Austin Energy access, and no license agreement is documented.

comments.title: Vault and Pedestal Locations Missing from Landscape Plan; Access Clearances Unverified
comments.comment: Electric vault, manhole, and pull box locations shown on the Electrical Design Plan are not overlaid on the Landscape Plan, making it impossible to verify that proposed trees and plantings maintain required clearances from vault covers and access openings.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.10.2 requires minimum 8-foot clearance in all directions around pedestals, subsurface vaults, and manholes requiring personnel access, and vault covers/lids must remain free of tree canopy obstruction to permit operational access. Vault easement, pull box, and manhole locations identified on Sheet 21 (including a labeled 'Vault Easement' west of Building 8 and multiple pull box locations north of Buildings 1, 3, 4, east of Building 6, and in the central corridor) do not appear on the Landscape Plan (Sheet 31). Without these locations shown on Sheet 31, neither tree canopy clearance from vault lids nor 8-foot obstruction-free access zones can be verified. Note: one run observed that the electrical plan shows pad-mounted transformers rather than subsurface Austin Energy vaults, creating some ambiguity about whether AE-owned subsurface facilities requiring this clearance are present.
comments.sheets: Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31); Site Plan (Sheet 9)
comments.applicableArea: All electric vault, manhole, and pull box locations throughout site; Vault Easement west of Building 8; pull box locations north of Buildings 1 and 3, northeast of Building 4, west of Building 2, east of Building 6, and central corridor
comments.resolution: Overlay all vault, manhole, and electrical pull box locations from Sheet 21 onto the Landscape Plan (Sheet 31). For each vault or manhole requiring personnel access, draw and dimension an 8-foot clearance zone and confirm that no proposed trees, shrubs, or other plantings are positioned within those zones or would overhang vault covers at mature canopy spread. If no Austin Energy-owned subsurface vaults are present (only customer-owned transformers), provide a note on Sheet 21 and Sheet 31 confirming this distinction and identifying which facilities, if any, are subject to the 8-foot access clearance requirement.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: One run found the plans show only pad-mounted (surface) transformers rather than subsurface Austin Energy vaults — reviewer should confirm whether Austin Energy-owned subsurface vaults requiring the 8-foot clearance are present on this project.

perRunFindings.comment: Unable to verify whether proposed trees block access to or overhang electric vaults due to lack of vault/manhole coordination on Landscape Plan.
applicableAreas: Electric vaults
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows pull boxes and transformers. Sheet 31 does not show pull boxes, vaults, or manhole locations. If subsurface electric equipment exists, its locations not depicted on Landscape Plan.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Cannot verify tree canopy clearance from vault lids without vault locations shown on Landscape Plan.

perRunFindings.comment: Show vault locations on the landscape plan with tree locations and estimated mature canopy spreads. Verify no trees are positioned to create overhead obstruction of vault covers/lids.
applicableAreas: Electric vault locations throughout site
perRunFindings.observation: Vault locations shown on Sheet 21 are not shown on landscape plan (Sheet 31). Vault covers/lids must remain clear of tree canopy for operational access, but without vault locations on the landscape plan, this cannot be verified.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 requires that vaults remain accessible for personnel and equipment. Trees positioned over vault covers prevent access operations. The landscape plan must show vault locations and tree canopy spreads to verify compliance.

perRunFindings.comment: Show vault and manhole locations from Sheet 21 on the landscape plan. Mark 8-foot clearance zones around each vault/manhole requiring personnel access and verify shrubs and obstructions are outside these zones.
applicableAreas: Subsurface electric vaults and manhole locations
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows vault and manhole locations (including a labeled 'Vault Easement' at transformer pad near Bldg. 8). Sheet 31 does not show these vault/manhole locations. Without them overlaid on the landscape plan, the required 8-foot clearance zone around vaults/manholes cannot be verified.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 requires minimum 8-foot clearance around all pedestals, subsurface vaults, or manholes requiring personnel access. The landscape plan must show vault/manhole locations to enable verification.

perRunFindings.comment: Electrical vaults, pedestals, and pull boxes are located throughout the site, but 8-foot clearances are not documented with dimensions or callouts. Provide plan views with dimensions and professional engineer certification verifying that a minimum 8-foot clearance in all directions is maintained around all pedestals, subsurface vaults, and electrical equipment requiring personnel access.
applicableAreas: electrical vault easement area west of Building 8
multiple electrical pull box locations throughout site
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) identifies a 'Vault Easement' on the west side of Building 8, with an adjacent 'Electrical Pull Box.' Multiple 'Electrical Pull Box' locations are marked throughout the site (north of Bldg. 1, north of Bldg. 3, northeast of Bldg. 4, west of Bldg. 2, central corridor, east of Bldg. 6, and others). No dimensions, clearance measurements, or distance callouts on Sheet 21 verify that structures, landscaping, or improvements maintain the required minimum 8-foot clearance around these pedestals, subsurface vaults, or equipment access points in all directions.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 requires 'minimum 8-foot clearance around all pedestals, subsurface vaults, or manholes requiring personnel access.' This is a quantified, measurable requirement. The site plan identifies multiple electrical vaults and pull boxes but provides no measurements or callouts demonstrating that the required 8-foot clearance is maintained.

perRunFindings.comment: Provide utility coordination documentation from Austin Energy identifying all subsurface vaults, pedestals, and maintenance access points. Ensure all structures and improvements maintain 8-foot minimum clearance from these access points in all directions.
applicableAreas: Pedestals, vaults, and manhole locations throughout site
perRunFindings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) identified four electrical transformer pad locations. These are pad-mounted (surface) units, not subsurface vaults. The plans do not show any underground pedestals, subsurface vaults, or Austin Energy maintenance access points (separate from building-owned transformers). The presence of subsurface Austin Energy electric vaults or pedestals requiring 8-foot personnel access clearance is not indicated on the electrical plans provided.
perRunFindings.reasoning: EL-5.25 requires: '8 feet of clearance from pedestals, subsurface Austin Energy vaults, or manholes that require personnel access.' The application shows distribution transformers but does not explicitly show or identify Austin Energy-owned subsurface vaults or pedestals separate from the building service infrastructure. Marked 'unclear' because the actual presence of Austin Energy vaults/pedestals requiring this clearance is not confirmed on available plans.

comments.title: Parking Area Proximity to Southern 5' Electric Easement Not Dimensioned
comments.comment: The site plan does not include dimension callouts confirming that the southern parking area and paved surfaces are fully outside the southern 5' Electric Easement boundary.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.10.2 prohibits parking lots, parking areas, covered parking structures, and paved surfaces within electric distribution easements.
